name: Start screen, example game and a saved game against the computer
description: The example game completes without blocking the primary action.
steps: Verify Play the computer is visible before scrolling. Observe cards entering from opposite edges and moving between fronts. Pause the example, verify it stops, then restart and play it.
Observe turns 1 through 12, scoring on turns 4, 8 and 12 and a 15–12 finish followed by an automatic fresh game.
Choose Easy, click Play the computer, tap King in your hand, tap the Left front and Lock in. After turn 2, reload, then choose Continue your game against the computer.
expected: Cards move inside the clipped board without fading. The loop restarts, and the saved turn survives reload.

name: Phone orders, scoring and spent cards
description: The phone layout keeps the hand and Lock in on screen and every order behaves as in the rules.
steps: Verify Play the computer is visible before scrolling. Pause the example and use Next demo turn through twelve turns; restart. Verify no page overflow.

Start a game. Turn 1 deploy King to Left. Turn 2 tap the King on Left, then Middle (Shift). Turn 3 tap the King on Middle, then Recall. Turn 4 deploy King to Right. Lock in each order and wait for the reveal.
Verify turn 5: Ace and 2 are spent as payments and the dashed King was spent after the turn-4 scoring. Open Moves so far and Rules, then close them.
expected: Hand and Lock in stay visible; movement, payment, scoring, recall and exhaustion are correct.

name: Online table across two players
description: Two separate browser contexts reveal only after both orders are locked in.
steps: Player A clicks Play a friend online and shares the link. Player B opens it in a separate context and clicks Join the game.
A deploys King to Left and locks in. B sees an empty board, no opposing order and a locked-in marker by A's name. B deploys Queen to Middle and locks in. Both advance to turn 2.
Reload both, choose Rejoin your online table, then Reconnect. Each deploys another legal card and locks in.
expected: Both recover their correct seat, see the same resolved board and scores, and advance live without leaking pending orders.

name: Pass and play with private handoffs
description: Local players keep simultaneous orders private and can finish a game.
steps: Choose Pass and play on this device. Player 1 taps I’m Player 1, deploys King to Left and locks in. Player 2 sees only a handoff, then an empty board after tapping I’m Player 2.
Player 2 deploys Queen to Middle and locks in. Tap Reveal both orders, then Next turn. Reload and choose Continue your pass-and-play game.
Finish the remaining turns, revealing together each time. At the result choose Play again.
expected: Orders stay concealed until the shared reveal, completed turns persist, and Play again starts a new game.

name: Guided lessons
description: Five lessons teach each order and end with a puzzle that has one winning order.
steps: Choose Learn by playing. Try a disallowed card and verify the refusal, then follow each lesson's instruction and choose Next lesson.
In lesson 5, shift the 6 to Left first and verify the reply beats it and the explanation names the answer. Choose Try again, shift the Jack from Right to Left and verify the win.
Finish and choose Play the computer (Easy).
expected: Each lesson accepts only its order, explains the result, and the puzzle accepts exactly one winning order.

name: Invalid invitations and room failures keep solo play available
covers: unavailable orders on an empty board
description: Failed online actions never block a game against the computer.
steps: Open an invitation link for a table that does not exist and choose Join the game; confirm the visible error. Return to the start screen, choose Play a friend online and confirm the injected error.
Start a game against the computer. Lock in is disabled until a card and a front are chosen.
Deploy King to Left and lock in. Return to the start screen, start again and choose Keep it. Continue the saved game.
expected: The saved turn is kept, errors are visible, and online failures do not prevent solo play.
